 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - V, Vijaypur (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal')
in MVC No.75/2013 vide its judgment and award dated 26.11.2015.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 09.09.2011 when he was riding his bicycle which was dashed against by a Tempo bearing registration No.MH- 14/F-5192 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').
The claimant claimed that he had suffered injuries on his face and that he had spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- for his treatment.
He therefore, filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the owner who claimed that the offending vehicle was sold by him on 07.01.2011 and therefore, he was not liable to pay any compensation.
The insurer denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimant for compensation.

Alternatively, it NC:
2023:KHC-K:5510 contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving licence.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P14.
He examined a doctor as PW.2 who assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 15% to 20% to the whole body.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 and R2.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also held that the claimant had suffered fracture of nasal bone and was hospitalized for 5 days.

It held that the claimant did not suffer any loss of income due to the disability and awarded the following compensation:-

The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant was employed and therefore, he was out of employment for nearly 2 to 3 months and therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal was not just and proper but is meager.
He also contended that the compensation under other heads warrants enhancement.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.

I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
10.

The Tribunal noticed the evidence of PW.2 who deposed that the fracture of the nasal bone would affect the other sensory functions and it is quite possible that the injuries suffered by the claimant could have caused immense loss of amenities.

Consequently, without going into the questions whether those injuries caused any disability to the claimant or whether he was out of employment due to the injuries, this Court considers it appropriate to enhance the compensation globally from Rs.1,00,000 to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/-.
11.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/-, which is payable by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
However, the claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 1309 days in filing this appeal.
